final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core predicates remain unresolved. The response is a narrower reinterpretation of the same record: aggregate readiness, reversible 3% rollout, and monitoring support a bounded operational posture, but they do not cure the compliance defect identified in the initial report. The distinction matters: a caveated description of weakness may justify calling the certification claim narrower, but it does not establish policy compliance when the affected use case remains exposed, approved risk acceptance is absent, and no completed prelaunch disclosure is in evidence. On the required concern accounting, none of the initial specific concerns were closed by genuinely new admissible evidence. Because the unresolved limitation still reaches a named launch use case and the policy text says rollout controls alone do not remove disclosure duties, the claim that the model can be certified for launch now remains unsupported on this record.
remaining_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate.
The risk acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so there is no approved risk acceptance covering the limitation.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no completed prelaunch disclosure is in evidence.
The governing policy text expressly states that a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
General public guidance about monitoring and model cards does not override the specific internal policy condition for launch.
